Each gate $g_i$ is an addition, subtraction or multiplication of two operands, each a constant in $F$, an input $a \in A$ or an earlier gate $g_j$ with $j < i$; an output operand is a constant in $F$, an input or any gate…
nodes.title: Arithmetic circuit

nodes.summary: An arithmetic gate over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ prior nodes is an addition, a subtraction or a multiplication of two arithmetic operands, each of which is a constant in $F$, an input $a \in A$ or a reference to a node $i < n$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic gate

nodes.summary: An arithmetic operand over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ nodes is a constant $x \in F$, an input $a \in A$, or a reference to a node $i < n$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic operand

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication, let $A$ be a type and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$ and a value in $F$ for each node $i < n$, write $v(x)$ for the value of an arithmetic operand $x$: a constant evaluates to itself, an input $a$ to its assigned value and a reference to node $i$ to the value given for node $i$. nodes.title: Gate evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication and let $c$ be an arithmetic circuit over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and outputs indexed by $B$. Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$, the value of $c$ at an output $b \in B$ is the value of the output operand of $b$, where a constant $x$ has value $x$, an input has its assigned value and a reference to gate $g_j$ has the value of $g_j$,…
nodes.title: Circuit evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication and let $c$ be an arithmetic circuit over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$. Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$, the value of gate $g_i$ of $c$ is the value of the operation of $g_i$ on its two operands, where a constant $x$ has value $x$, an input has its assigned value and a reference to an earlier gate $g_j$ with $j < i$ takes the value of…
nodes.title: Value of a gate in a circuit

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $A$ be types and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Given a value in $F$ for each input $a \in A$ and a value in $F$ for each node $i < n$, an arithmetic operand over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and $n$ nodes evaluates as follows: a constant $x$ evaluates to $x$, an input $a$ to its assigned value, and a reference to node $i$ to the value given for node $i$.
nodes.title: Operand evaluation

nodes.summary: Two arithmetic circuits over $F$ with inputs indexed by $A$ and outputs indexed by $B$ are equal if they have the same size, the same gate at each position and the same output operand for each $b \in B$.
nodes.title: Extensionality for arithmetic circuits

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a type with addition, subtraction and multiplication. For all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, $a \in F^m$, $b \in F^n$, $i < m$ and $j < n$, the outer-product circuit over $F$ evaluated on the inputs $a$ and $b$ has value $a_i b_j$ at the output $(i, j)$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the outer-product circuit

nodes.summary: For every $F$ and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product circuit over $F$ for $m \times n$ outer products has exactly $mn$ gates.
nodes.title: Size of the outer-product circuit

nodes.summary: For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product circuit has inputs $a_0, \dots, a_{m-1}$ and $b_0, \dots, b_{n-1}$, one output for each pair $(i, j)$ with $i < m$ and $j < n$, and exactly $mn$ gates: the gate for $(i, j)$ multiplies $a_i$ by $b_j$, and the output at $(i, j)$ is that gate.
nodes.title: Outer-product circuit

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
